comments.author: halotrope
comments.story_title: Ask HN: What are some good resources to learn how electricity works?
comments.why_zh: 为软件工程师把电学与现代计算机联系起来。
comments.quote_zh: 在把电学和现代计算机联系起来这件事上非常有帮助
comments.text_zh: 我发现 Ben Eater 的“Hello world from scratch”[1] 系列在把电学和现代计算机联系起来这件事上非常有帮助。严格来说它讲的是电子学，但从“普通”软件工程视角来看，它的呈现非常出色，也极具启发性。真正让我找到它的是 Charles Petzold 的《Code》[2]，这本书追溯了从灯泡、电报线等早期电路到现代数字逻辑的发展。我发现，在接触这些概念之后，再学习基础物理会容易理解得多，因为它被放在了当代应用的语境中。1: [VIDEO] 2: [LINK]
comments.text: I found the „Hello world from scratch“[1] series from Ben Eater incredibly helpful in connecting the dots between electricity and modern computers. Strictly speaking it is about electronics, still it is superbly presented and incredibly enlightening when coming from „normal“ software engineering perspective of things. What actually got me there was the book „Code“ by Charles Petzold[2] which traces the development from early circuitry like light bulbs and telegraph wires to modern digital logic. I found that after being introduced to these concepts, learning about the fundamental physics was much more accessible since it was framed in the context of contemporary application. 1: [VIDEO] 2: [LINK]

comments.author: halotrope
comments.story_title: Fritzing is an open-source electronic design tool
comments.why_zh: 关于基础电子学和计算机的初学者教程。
comments.quote_zh: 或者 Ben Eater 那套出色的初学者教程
comments.text_zh: 如果 fritzing 在 HN 上拿到第 1 名，我也想真心推荐 [LINK]。依我看，最新版本的工作流程合理得多，用户体验也很好。我做了一块简单的 PCB，在 [LINK] 上花了几美元就把它制造出来了。相当有成就感的一次体验。我也会建议任何关心计算机的人都去了解基础电子学。晶体管是怎么工作的，总线（比如 I2C 或 SPI）是什么，以及这一切是怎么连接起来的？（鼓点……当然是一块 PCB）。YouTube 上有大量从头到尾完整演示的教程。比如 Phils Lab [LINK] 讲 PCB 设计。或者 Ben Eater 那套出色的初学者教程“Hello World from Scratch” [VIDEO]
comments.text: If fritzing gets #1 spot on HN I would like to wholeheartedly recommend [LINK] as well. IMHO much saner workflow and good UX in the latest version.I did a simple PCB and got it manufactured on [LINK] for a couple bucks. Quite a rewarding experience. I would also suggest that anyone who cares about computers gets to know basic electronics. How do transistors work, what is a bus (e.g I2C or SPI) and how is it all connected? (Drumroll ... a PCB of course). There is a ton of tutorials on youtube that do it end to end. E.g Phils Lab [LINK] for a PCB design. Or Ben Eaters excellent beginner tutorial "Hello World from Scratch" [VIDEO]

comments.author: Joel_Mckay
comments.story_title: Ask HN: Books to learn 6502 ASM and the Apple II
comments.why_zh: 与高级语言不同，它展示了 CPU 实际在做什么。
comments.quote_zh: 强烈建议从简单的架构开始。
comments.text_zh: 我难以苟同，不过还是尊重你的看法：BASIC/Java/Arduino 向用户隐藏了太多关于 CPU 如何工作的细节。从 Ben Eater 那里买一套 6502 套件，并逐步梳理 CPU 是如何工作的，会隐含地展示出各种语言是如何把实际发生的事情抽象掉的。更重要的是，还能获得理解如何编写高效程序所必需的技能。[VIDEO] [LINK] 强烈建议从简单的架构开始。=3
comments.text: I respectfully disagree, BASIC/Java/Arduino hides too much about how the CPU works from users. Getting a 6502 kit from Ben Eater, and walking though how the CPU works will implicitly show how languages abstracted away whats actually happening. And more importantly, the skills necessary to understand how to write efficient programs. [VIDEO] [LINK] Starting with a simple architecture is highly recommended. =3
